chunks: My father narrated to us, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, who said: A man came to al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), and said: O son of Allah's Messenger, inform me about the noblest of moral traits.
So he said: Pardoning those who wronged you, connecting with those who disconnected from you, giving those who prevented you, and saying the truth, even if it may be against yourself.
ai.seo_question: What are the four key traits of noble character according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* highlights the Imam’s definition of *makarim al-akhlaq* (noble character) as active, counter-intuitive virtues that transcend mere reciprocity. By commanding forgiveness, kinship maintenance, generosity, and self-honesty, the Imam aligns ethical conduct with the Shia ideal of *ihsan* (excellence in worship and behavior), reflecting the spiritual maturity expected of the faithful. These principles serve as practical applications of the Quranic call to repel evil with good, reinforcing the social cohesion central to the Ahl al-Bayt’s teachings.
